item.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga set for emotional Athletic Club homecoming at San Mames as Arsenal backup goalkeeper is called up by Basque Country to face Venezuela
item.description: Girona FC v Arsenal FC - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised for a poignant return to former club Athletic Club's San Mames stadium after earning a call-up from the Basque Country representative team. The shot-stopper has been named in the Euskal Selekzioa squad to take on South American visitors Venezuela during next weekend's international friendly in Bilbao. Record-breaking keeper returns to Bilbao Osasuna manager Jagoba Arrasate has included the Ondarroa native as one of the marquee names in his 22-man selection for the clash on Saturday, November 14. Currently serving as understudy to David Raya at Arsenal following previous loan stints with Real Madrid and Bournemouth, Arrizabalaga originally departed Bilbao for Chelsea in 2018. That €80 million move to Stamford Bridge remains the world-record transfer fee ever paid for a goalkeeper. Foreign-based trio join domestic core Joining Arrizabalaga in the squad as players plying their trade outside Spain are Udinese forward Unai Gomez and Bolton Wanderers attacker Gaizka Larrazabal, while Osasuna stopper Aitor Fernandez provides competition between the posts. Arrasate has once again leaned heavily on a familiar domestic core drawn from Athletic Club, Real Sociedad, Osasuna and Deportivo Alaves. In defence, Athletic's Dani Vivian, Hugo Rincon and Johaneko Louis-Jean are joined by Sociedad trio Jon Pacheco, Igor Zubeldia and Aihen Munoz alongside Osasuna's Inigo Arguibide and Malaga's Einar Galilea. Midfield options feature Athletic's Mikel Jauregizar, Sociedad's Benat Turrientes, Alaves pair Pablo Ibanez and Ander Guevara, Osasuna's Asier Osambela and Sevilla's Jon Guridi, while Athletic star Oihan Sancet, Osasuna's Kike Barja and Racing Santander duo Inigo Vicente and Asier Villalibre complete the attack. Historic friendly honours cultural ties Organised by Basque Football Federation president Xabier Goni, the fixture marks the representative team's first appearance since defeating Palestine 3-0 in front of a record 51,396 crowd on November 15 last year via goals from Unai Elgezabal, Gorka Guruzeta and Urko Izeta. Next Saturday's contest carries deep cultural weight as it celebrates the 90th anniversary of the first autonomous Basque Government formed under President Jose Antonio Aguirre in 1936. Aguirre subsequently established the Euzkadi team in 1937 to tour Europe and the Americas during the Spanish Civil War. Venezuela also holds a special bond with the region after welcoming thousands of Basque political exiles fleeing Francisco Franco's dictatorship. item.title: Aleksandar Pavlović wants to win everything with Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Stefan Matzke - sampics/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aleksandar Pavlović is not interested in setting modest targets for Bayern Munich this season. The young midfielder has made it clear that the expectations inside the dressing room are as high as ever, with the club aiming to co mpete for every major trophy available. Asked about Bayern’s objectives for the campaign, Pavlović delivered a straightforward answer that should sound familiar to anyone who understands the expectations at the Allianz Arena “We want to win everything: the Champions League, the DFB-Pokal and the Bundesliga title,” Pavlović told Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). There is no shortage of ambition in those words, but Bayern Munich has the squad and quality to make those aspirations realistic. The Bundesliga remains the club’s domestic priority, and Vincent Kom pany will expect his team to maintain its consistency over the course of a demanding league campaign. Bayern also has unfinished business in the DFB-Pokal, a competition they have not won since 2020. Ending that drought would be another important milestone for this group. Then there is the Champions League, the ultimate measuring stick for any Bayern Munich side. Winning the competition re quires more than individual brilliance. It demands consistency, resilience, tactical discipline, and the ability to deliver when the pres sure is at its highest. For Pavlović, these are not simply lofty aspirations. They are the standards expected at Bayern Munic h. The midfielder has grown into an increasingly important part of the squad, and his mentality reflects the club’s ambitions. Wi nning one trophy would represent a successful season for many clubs. At Bayern, the expectation is to chase all th ree. Pavlović clearly understands that distinction. item.title: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid Barcelona could also turn to Gavi for Sunday’s LaLiga meeting with Atletico Madrid, although Marc Bernal and Frenkie de Jong remain stronger candidates to replace the injured Rodri, reports Mundo Deportivo For now, manager Hansi Flick has several midfield alternatives available for this clash, with the decision likely to depend on multiple factors, including experience and form. This situation arrives as Rodri has been ruled out after medical tests confirmed a minor injury to his right hamstring. Barcelona announced on November 4 that the midfielder would miss the crucial La Liga fixture, leaving Flick with an important selection decision ahead of the trip to the Metropolitano. Gavi’s inclusion in the discussion is particularly interesting given his experience in high-pressure matches and his ability to adapt to different midfield roles. However, it is crucial to note that the 22-year-old should not be considered the leading candidate at this stage. Bernal and De Jong lead Barcelona’s midfield options Marc Bernal has solid grounds to replace Rodri. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As reported before, though, Bernal is the most natural replacement for Rodri . The academy graduate has already demonstrated his suitability for the role, having started against Elche, Athletic Club, Rayo Vallecano and Paris Saint-Germain this season. Furthermore, De Jong is another possibility after recovering from his injury problems. The Dutchman returned during the Clasico and subsequently started against Alaves, although he was a substitute against Aston Villa. His experience and ability to control possession offer Flick a different profile from Bernal. Gavi’s experience in decisive matches gives Flick a strong option Gavi’s case is built on his performances during the closing stages of Barcelona’s previous campaign. After recovering from his serious knee injury, the midfielder became an important option for Flick in several demanding fixtures, demonstrating that he could be trusted when the stakes were high. Gavi will bring a different profile than Frenkie de Jong and Bernal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He featured in the Catalan derby against Espanyol, where he operated as a left winger, before starting in tricky away encounters against Osasuna and Getafe. He also played as a central midfielder in El Clasico against Real Madrid, the match in which Barcelona mathematically secured the La Liga title. Those appearances showed Gavi’s tactical flexibility and competitive intensity. His ability to press aggressively, recover possession, and support attacking transitions gives Flick a different midfield profile from both Bernal and De Jong. item.title: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break
item.description: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break Schalke will hope to end their abysmal run before the international break as they face fellow strugglers Hoffenheim away from home. Hoffenheim After three away games in a week, Christian Ilzer's men will be back at SNP Arena on Sunday night. The Sinsheim side failed to win those fixtures in three different competitions. The defeat in Bremen ended a two-game winning streak in Bundesliga, days after they were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal by 2. Bundesliga outfit Holstein Kiel. And, on Thursday, they were very close to upset Europa Conference League winners Crystal Palace before an injury-time strike by former Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Daichi Kamada undone them. However, Hoffenheim won their last two home games 3-0 against Lyon and Bayer Leverkusen. Team News Adam Hložek and Vladimir Coufal weren't in the traveling squad in London, but they both could make their return on Sunday. Alexander Prass, who scored Hoffenheim's goal against Palace, will be back after missing last week's defeat to Bremen due to suspension. Schalke Since the return of club football from October's international break, Schalke 04 have only picked up a single point in the Bundesliga. Miron Muslić’s men were also knocked out of the cup by 2. Bundesliga club Dynamo Dresden as they only scored one goal in their last six competitive games. On matchday 8, Schalke’s search for a first home goal was unsuccessful as they were dominated from start to finish by RB Leipzig, who lost all their previous away matches until that point. Schalke’s next two games at Veltins Arena will also be against Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Dortmund. item.title: How will Barcelona line up against Atlético Madrid?
item.description: Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images | Getty Images Barcelona look to go into the final international break of the season with a statement win in the bag as the La Liga leaders travel to the capital for a monster top of the table clash against Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano . Here’s how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Sunday’s battle: Defense Barça are expecting to have an almost fully healthy and fit squad after the break if there are no issues during the international window, and they will also have Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen in the squad for Sunday. But the two defenders have not trained long enough to be ready to start, so we expect the same back four in front of Joan Garcia that kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa: Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín at center-back, João Cancelo at left-back, and Brian Fariñas , who continues to impress since getting his first opportunity last weekend, starting at right-back. Midfield Barça will be without Rodri with a minor hamstring issue and there’s a real doubt about who will Flick choose to partner Pedri and Fermín López . Marc Bernal had a strong substitute cameo as Rodri’s replacement in midweek and has been Flick’s first backup choice to the Spain captain so far this season, but Frenkie de Jong is back to 100% and ready to step back into his favorite midfield role. We think Flick will go with the Dutchman for this one, which will likely cause a slight change of formation with a double pivot of Frenkie and Pedri and Fermín as the number 10. Attack Lamine Yamal and Raphinha shined against Villa and will be looking for another big night against Atlético’s tough defense, and we think Flick will once again trust Anthony Gordon ahead of Karim Adeyemi for this one. Possible XI : Joan; Fariñas, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; De Jong, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Gordon; Raphinha (4-2-3-1) How do you think Barcelona should line up against Atlético Madrid? item.title: Ilia Topuria Credits Brother For Saving MMA Career At UFC’s White House Card
item.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria is lucky to still have a fighting career after the damage he sustained at UFC’s White House card earlier this year and he owes it all to his brother. It’s only been five months since Topuria lost his UFC lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at Freedom 250 back in June, but it certainly seems longer. Topuria was a massive betting favorite to essentially punch his way past Gaethje and cement himself as the next big superstar in the sport. While Topuria is still young enough and talented enough to reclaim his 155-pound throne his star power took a serious hit. Fortunately, Topuria didn’t sustain any career-altering injuries from his brawl with “Highlight.” Gaethje did massive damage in the later rounds of the fight that basically left Topuria unrecognizable, but if it wasn’t for Topuria’s brother, Aleksandre Topuria, he may have left the White House lawn with permanent damage to his vision. Luckily, his brother stopped the fight before the start of the fifth round to save Topuria from any further punishment. It wasn’t the most popular decision, but certainly the right one. Topuria, who has recovered well and aiming for a return to action in early 2027 , credits his brother for saving his career that night in Washington D.C. Without him, Topuria doesn’t know if he would have been able to fight again. Check it out below: Ilia Topuria says he's grateful that his brother stopped him from taking more damage against Justin Gaethje: "If he wouldn't stop the fight, probably I wouldn't be able to fight again in my life. I'm so grateful with my brother." (via @AdamCatterall ) pic.twitter.com/T8nDaTfQp2 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 6, 2026 “If he hadn’t stopped me from fighting, I probably wouldn’t have been able to fight again in my life,” said Topuria during a recent interview with Adam Catterall (shown above). “I’m so grateful to my brother for deciding to stop me because I love what I’m doing. I had a bad experience, but I still have a lot ahead of me. It would be very sad to hear from a doctor or anyone that I wouldn’t be able to fight anymore.”

item.title: Lott takes over in Lady Rebels' dominant first win
item.description: UNLV Lady Rebels guard Jasmyn Lott (10) draws an and-one during the first half of a college basketball game against UTSA on Friday, November 6 2026 at Cox Pavilion in Las Vegas, Nevada. LAS VEGAS – Redshirt senior guard Jasmyn Lott is one of two players on the current Lady Rebels roster who shared the floor with program great Desi-Rae Young (Class of 2024). Therefore, it was only fitting that Lott stole the show on a night when Young’s No. 23 jersey was retired. Lott followed up the pregame celebrations with a game-high 22-point performance — one point shy of tying her career high — to lead UNLV to a dominant 69-51 victory over the University of Texas-San Antonio (UTSA) in its home curtain raiser. Lott spoke about how much her relationship with Young means to her afterward and that extra fire in her belly may have inadvertently helped her break out of a bit of a slump. “Nobody deserves it more than her,” Lott said. “[Young] is UNLV. I’ve looked up to her since [I was a freshman]. I really love her a lot, and I wish her nothing but the best.” Lott led the Lady Rebels in scoring with 9 points at halftime before taking over the game with an 11-point third quarter. UNLV outscored its visitors 26-16 in the period to take a cozy 53-37 advantage into the last 10 minutes. The Frisco, Texas native shot 6-for-13 from the field (3-for-7 3PT) and a perfect 7-for-7 at the line. She looked like anything but a player lacking confidence. Yet this type of outing might have been exactly what she needed to open the floodgates offensively. “I don’t really go into any game thinking this is going to be my night,” Lott said. “I’ve been struggling with my confidence a lot, so I just kind of try to help my team as best as I can.” A smile beamed from Lott’s face when she was asked how it felt to see her shots fall regularly tonight. “Much better,” she added. “It kind of alleviated some of the pressure that I put on myself with everything I do.” Although the Lady Rebels ended up winning by 18 — improving to 1-1 on the year — they needed every bit of Lott’s shot-making to stay afloat early. UNLV shot poorly in the first quarter. At one point, they were 2-for-18 from the field and went into the break shooting 9-for-35. However, they found some rhythm in the second frame, edging in front for a 27-21 lead. Despite the struggles, head coach Lindy La Rocque was pleased with what her team was doing offensively and believed it would turn into points eventually. She was right. “I thought we got some good looks. We missed a couple of easy layups that we’d like back, and the threes that we were taking I was happy with, and they just weren’t going in,” La Rocque said. “[UTSA] was really packing the paint and honestly, a shot attempt is better than a turnover, so I was proud that we were getting our shots up.” La Rocque trusted her shooters and her entire team entered a flow state after the interval. item.title: “He will deliver” – Andoni Iraola heaps praise on in-form Liverpool star
item.description: “He will deliver” – Andoni Iraola heaps praise on in-form Liverpool star Andoni Iraola Backs Alexander Isak as Liverpool’s Reliable Goal Threat Alexander Isak has started the season doing what elite strikers are paid to do, score goals. Seven already, the latest coming off the bench in the Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce, and Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola sounds like a man who knows exactly what he has. His verdict was direct. “Alex is a top goalscorer,” said Iraola. “If we can put him in the position to score, he will deliver. It’s not a guarantee but it’s the closest thing to a guarantee almost.” That tells you plenty. Liverpool do not need Isak to be everything at once. They need him where it matters, in the right areas, finishing moves. Alexander Isak giving Liverpool clarity in attack Iraola’s comments also showed what Liverpool are trying to build around the Sweden international. He praised the striker’s movement and technical quality, saying: “Like every player, he can add more things to his game. We want to use the things that he has, he is very good also attacking the spaces, attacking the channels, coming to receive [the ball]. I think he is technically clean also. “We are trying to use him in the best way.” Photo: IMAGO That is sensible coaching. Isak’s game is not limited to penalty-box finishing. He can stretch defences, run the channels and link play cleanly. For Liverpool, that matters because it gives the front line more variety and makes him harder to mark. Bradley Barcola role offers Iraola another option Iraola was also asked about Bradley Barcola, who operated through the middle in Turkiye rather than from his usual wide role. The answer was clear enough. “Bradley is a winger. “Mostly he has played as a left winger, sometimes as a right winger, but he also has played in PSG as a striker. “It’s something that I wanted to try. I thought against their centre-backs he could be a threat, especially in behind. “But he is a winger and he will be mostly, 90 per cent of the time, used as a winger. But it’s alternatives that I sometimes want to try. I tried with Cody [Gakpo] against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup. “Not maybe from the beginning but it’s true that during the game, I think it’s options that we can use when Alex is tired and we need another type of striker. “We can use other strikers that we have but also wingers can do a job there.” Liverpool attack built around options and efficiency That is the bigger point. Iraola has a first-choice striker in Alexander Isak and he knows it. He also wants flexible attacking cover when matches shift. Barcola through the middle is an option, not a change of identity. Liverpool’s attack still revolves around getting Isak the ball in decisive spaces. On current form, that remains the smartest plan available.

item.title: ‘It was all of us’: Usman Khawaja drops bombshell on Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has made fresh revelations about the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, claiming that discussions about altering the ball were far more widespread within the team than Cricket Australia's investigation established. In excerpts from his upcoming autobiography published by the Sydney Morning Herald on Saturday, Khawaja alleged that conversations about ball-tampering took place openly during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa. He claimed players discussed different ways of roughing up the ball, including using sandpaper, in what he described as "open, lighthearted discussions". The former top-order batter further suggested that the conversations were not restricted to a particular group within the dressing room, insisting that players across different departments and support staff were aware of them. "It was all of us," Khawaja said in the book, according to the newspaper. The revelations have raised fresh questions about the findings of Cricket Australia's investigation into the scandal, which erupted during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. The controversy, widely known as 'Sandpapergate', triggered one of the biggest integrity crises in Australian cricket after players were caught using sandpaper to tamper with the ball. Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that prior knowledge of the plan was limited to three players: Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Khawaja, who featured in 88 Tests for Australia, was cleared of any wrongdoing during the investigation. He announced his retirement from international cricket in January. Cricket Australia stands by 2018 investigation Responding to the latest claims, Cricket Australia defended its investigation and maintained that its findings remained valid. "All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process," the governing body said in a statement on Saturday. It also stressed that there had always been an opportunity for individuals to provide additional information. "There has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case," it added. Following the 2018 investigation, Cricket Australia handed playing bans and other penalties to Smith, Warner and Bancroft. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but stepped down shortly after the series. Cummins had played down possibility of fresh fallout Australia captain Pat Cummins, who was part of the bowling attack in the infamous Cape Town Test, had earlier played down suggestions that Khawaja's autobiography could reignite the controversy or lead to further consequences when it was released. item.title: Non-league's greatest giant-killers eye another scalp
item.description: "I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible." With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity. One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions. Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football. During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982. 'We had this determination' "It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport. Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions." Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, twice helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division opponents; Everton at Goodison Park in 1975, and then a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979. An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. This was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups? "We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. "You reach your level in football, but on a one-off occasion you'd be astonished at where you can raise your game to. You can't do it every week, but it's just a case of getting the mindset right on the day." The club may also have been fuelled by a sense of injustice. item.description: Ryan Warsofsky Sharks Getty San Jose Sharks head coach Ryan Warsofsky is on thin ice after the team lost another game and further sank in the Western Conference. With a 4-1 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Friday night, the Sharks dropped to 7-10-1 on the season, an extremely disappointing start to the season for a San Jose team that was supposed to take a giant leap forward and make a playoff push this season. That’s why Warsofsky, who is in his third season as San Jose’s coach, has to be on thin ice. Ryan Warsofsky’s Seat Is Getting Warmer The Sharks are now in sixth place in the Pacific Division, ahead of only the Los Angeles Kings and the Vancouver Canucks, and they are now behind the Calgary Flames, which is not a place that the Sharks expected to be heading into this season given all of the offseason moves that GM Mike Grier made to improve the team and make a playoff push. According to TSN NHL insider Pierre LeBrun , the Sharks are not considering a coaching change at this time. But they can’t keep waiting around forever, as it’s always easier to fire the coach than to change the players. “The Sharks are near the bottom in goals for. They’re near the bottom in goals against. It’s ugly. The team’s struggles have led to speculation about Ryan Warsofsky. My understanding is that Sharks GM Mike Grier is not contemplating a coaching change at this stage,” LeBrun said. Macklin Celebrini Deserves Better Sharks superstar Macklin Celebrini is one of the best players in the entire NHL, but he deserves better than what his San Jose team is doing right now. There was so much excitement heading into this season, with Celebrini being named the team captain and the club acquiring veterans such as Jacob Trouba, Darnell Nurse, and Mason Marchment. But for whatever reason, it’s not adding up to wins right now, as the Sharks have been nothing but an utter disappointment. Maybe Warsofsky gets another week to turn things around. But Grier and the Sharks’ front office won’t wait around forever for improvement. item.title: Devils stay top with overtime victory against Stars
item.description: Cardiff Devils wore a one-off bespoke uniform, with the game against Dundee Stars designated 'country night'. [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November. Visiting netminder Vladislav Pestov finished with 53 saves for the Stars who frustrated a dominant home side with a resolute defensive display. Dundee opened the scoring in the first period through Matthew DeBoer, after a breakaway from a Devils error. The home side finally found a way through with a Brandon Estes shot from point to equalise midway through the second. Neither side could force a regulation winner, and there were just 40 seconds left on the clock in overtime when Kristoff Kontos scored his first league goal of the season to claim the extra point for Cardiff. "It's two points, it's a win," said a relieved Devils head coach Paul Thompson. "We didn't make the most of the [offensive] zone time that we had from a scoring perspective, but I'm happy that Kontos made that big play to score us the OT winner." Cardiff - who have 13 points, the same as second placed Sheffield Steelers - travel to Fife Flyers on Sunday, 8 November (17:00 GMT).
